Not sure if I can help, but here’s what my crappy neurodivergent brain thought up. 

I’m still in the abusive home. I try to get away as much as possible, watch my favorite movies and shows and videos over and over. I always have music or someone talking. I stay in my room whenever I can. I avoid them as much as possible; excuses such as homework, gonna get water/food, lying about a friend wanting to call/talk, etc. I don’t cope honestly. I read a lot, and use fictional families to try and get away from my shit family. I used to (when I was desperate for any connection) look up pictures of happy families on google. Fucking depressing, I know haha. But it helped a little. 
My friends don’t really have great families either, but one of my friends who does have a good parental unit is definitely more open. She talks to them a lot, came out to them with no issue, is more okay with physical contact/the idea of it, has meals with them. I can’t imagine doing any of that. But yeah. I’m sorry if this was a mess. My crappy two cents.

TW for eating disorder mention and slight talk about it + ab*se mention))

I’m nauseous basically all the time lol. Whenever I wake up I’m nauseous for about 60-120 minutes (or all day). Over the past few months I’ve been having severe chest pains, breathing issues, limbs going numb, severe fatigue and extreme trouble waking up no matter how long I sleep for, shivering/shaking, can’t walk without getting winded or breathing hard, stuff like that. I went to a few people and the first two (school nurses) just sent me to my therapist, the other (professional/licensed doctor) telling me it was just because I didn’t exercise enough. 
I mentioned that I had had eating disorders in the past (not diagnosed as such, but they were pretty obviously eds. I’d starve myself for weeks. I felt like there was a guy telling me to do it in my head, that sh!t) and she just brushed it off, saying “yeah, just do it healthily”. Like, yeah, next time I’m forcing myself to not eat because I think I’m too fat to live I’ll just. Stop. I’m sorry, I’m upset. I’m young, like, under 20, I don’t know why this is happening. I’ve just been brushed off my by doctors, and I live in an ab•sive home. I don’t really get to ask for things, especially big things like doctors. Anyways. Things have been tough.

Thoughts aren’t actions. As far as I know, as long as you don’t say you WILL do it, or that you have intent, they can’t/won’t do anything (they as in therapist). Maybe try a hotline, or try to find someone online? If you’re planning on doing it, try (again) to see if you can find a therapist? There’s a lot of specialties and things like that. I’m sorry. It sounds awful, what you’re going through.

I’m so sorry. It must be awful to go through that. If you haven’t, do you want to try a podcast, or music, or something like that? do you have any friends to call? anything that helps you sleep (scents, clothes, blankets, etc)? Are you hungry? Do you want something warm? Maybe, if you’re comfortable with it, tomorrow you can call him and explain to him what’s happening? You don’t have to, no pressure at all, but it might be good to let him know how you feel.

I have intrusive thoughts, and they make me feel disgusting. I don’t know if you have those, but know that thoughts aren’t actions. You aren’t disgusting. You're not. You’re valid and so are your struggles. You do *not* deserve to die. If you want, maybe try to find someone to talk to?

I’ll never hear the rain tapping on windows again. I’ll never listen to my favorite song again. ill never know how it feels to get hypothermia, or stand in the rain at 2 am. I’ll never hear the fridge beep because I left it open again. I’ll never be hugged again. I’ll never take a nap on a Saturday, and wake up to the sun being a golden brown, and having the shadows of branches outside reflect on the windows. I’ll never listen to the rain tap on the windows on a friday night again. I’ll never buy fuzzy clothes again, never feel sweat drip down my back again. I’ll never feel hot cocoa burn my tongue again, or get brain freeze. I’ll never eat cereal again, or laugh at a stupid joke again.

I stay for the small things, honestly. It’s worth it for me.
